long_biography.plain_text:
Pamukçu began Tekboy with three tonnes of daily yarn-dyeing capacity. Over the following decades, he added knitted-fabric dyeing in Yenibosna, rotary printing and a large Lüleburgaz plant. By the time he discussed the business with Turkey's textile-finishing trade journal, it employed about 600 people and operated 23,000 square metres of factory space. Tekboy had also entered the country's thousand largest industrial companies.

His training as a chemical engineer also led him outside conventional textiles. In 2009 he established Dermotek to develop plant-based hair, skin and personal-care products, and he backed the formation of Biotek Biotechnology. The latter combined agricultural propagation with research into plant-derived cosmetic and pharmaceutical ingredients, extending his manufacturing interests from fabric chemistry towards life-science applications.
